content: For delivery delays, immediately contact logistics partner to track shipment location. Provide customer with updated ETA and offer 10% discount on next order if delay exceeds 3 days. Escalate to operations manager if delay is over 7 days.

Standard protocol for late deliveries: 1) Verify current shipment status, 2) Contact carrier for explanation, 3) Inform customer within 2 hours, 4) Offer expedited shipping on replacement if needed, 5) Apply service credit of $50-200 based on order value.

Delivery delay resolution process: Check warehouse dispatch logs, verify carrier pickup time, identify bottleneck (warehouse/transit/last-mile), communicate transparently with customer, offer compensation based on delay severity and customer tier.

Damaged goods protocol: Request photo evidence from customer, file claim with shipping carrier within 24 hours, arrange immediate replacement shipment, offer 20% discount or full refund. Document damage patterns for supplier feedback.

For damaged shipments: 1) Assess damage extent via photos, 2) Approve immediate replacement for orders >$500, 3) Investigate packaging quality with supplier, 4) Update packaging requirements if pattern detected, 5) Compensate customer with credit or refund.

Handle damaged goods by: Collecting visual evidence, determining if damage occurred in transit or at origin, coordinating with QA team for supplier evaluation, processing refund/replacement within 48 hours, implementing corrective measures.

Pricing discrepancy resolution: Verify contract pricing in system, compare with invoice, issue credit memo if overcharged, update pricing master data, notify customer within 24 hours with corrected invoice and apology.

For billing errors: 1) Pull original quote and contract terms, 2) Identify source of error (manual entry/system/contract update), 3) Issue immediate credit adjustment, 4) Send corrected invoice, 5) Flag account for audit if recurring issue.

Pricing error protocol: Validate customer's claimed price against agreement, check for promotional pricing or volume discounts, correct invoice in billing system, process refund to original payment method, document error for process improvement.

Missing items procedure: Cross-check packing list with warehouse pick ticket, verify actual shipment weight, ship missing items via express at no charge, apply $25-100 service credit, investigate warehouse picking accuracy.

For incomplete orders: 1) Confirm missing items from packing documentation, 2) Expedite shipment of missing items within 24 hours, 3) Waive shipping charges, 4) Offer 15% discount on affected items, 5) Review warehouse processes if pattern emerges.

Resolution for short shipments: Verify inventory allocation, check for picking errors, immediately dispatch missing quantity, compensate for inconvenience with credit, conduct root cause analysis with warehouse team.

Communication complaint resolution: Assign dedicated account manager, provide direct contact details, commit to 4-hour response time SLA, send daily updates until issue resolved, offer service credit for inconvenience.

For communication failures: 1) Acknowledge complaint immediately, 2) Escalate to customer success manager, 3) Establish direct communication channel, 4) Provide hourly updates on critical issues, 5) Implement communication improvement plan.

Handle communication issues by: Apologizing for delay, assigning senior support specialist, providing multiple contact channels (phone/email/chat), setting clear expectations for response times, following up proactively.

Quality complaint protocol: Request detailed description and photos, arrange immediate replacement, initiate supplier quality audit, offer full refund plus 25% credit, document issue for supplier scorecard review.

For quality concerns: 1) Collect evidence (photos, samples if possible), 2) Issue immediate replacement shipment, 3) Notify supplier quality team, 4) Conduct root cause analysis, 5) Implement corrective action with supplier, 6) Compensate customer generously.

Quality issue resolution: Validate complaint with quality team, determine if isolated incident or batch problem, recall affected inventory if needed, provide premium replacement, strengthen quality checks with supplier.

Documentation error handling: Identify missing/incorrect documents, coordinate with compliance team to generate correct paperwork, send via express courier if urgent, waive any delay-related charges, update document checklist.

For paperwork issues: 1) Determine which documents are incorrect, 2) Generate corrected versions within 4 hours, 3) Send digitally and via courier, 4) Coordinate with customs broker if needed, 5) Prevent recurrence through process update.

Missing documentation protocol: Verify required certificates for product/region, obtain from supplier or quality team, provide digital copies immediately, mail originals overnight, add to shipment checklist for future orders.

Service complaint resolution: Apologize sincerely, investigate incident with involved staff, offer service recovery (discount/credit), assign different representative for future interactions, implement coaching for staff member.

For unprofessional behavior: 1) Take complaint seriously and apologize, 2) Investigate with employee and supervisor, 3) Provide immediate service recovery ($50-150 credit), 4) Ensure different staff handles account, 5) Conduct training if needed.

Handle service issues by: Acknowledging customer's negative experience, investigating circumstances, taking corrective action with employee, offering meaningful compensation, assigning senior team member to rebuild relationship.
